title: Sos Pomidorowy (Tomato Sauce)
description: A sauce made with tomatoes, broth or bouillon, and butter.
steps: Chop six medium tomatoes and stew them in butter, moistening with broth or bouillon.

Then add one teaspoon of sugar.
Make a white roux separately with one teaspoon of butter and a little flour, add to the tomatoes, mix well and dilute with strong broth or bouillon to the right consistency.
Finally bring to a boil and pour over meat.

title: Sos Rakowy (Crayfish Sauce)
description: A sauce made with crayfish, white pepper, and broth or bouillon.
steps: Pound cooked crayfish shells in a mortar, place in a small pot, add butter and stew on gentle heat.
Crayfish butter will form on the surface, which should be carefully collected with a spoon.
Two tablespoons of this butter boil on gentle heat with one tablespoon flour.
Add one tablespoon of good raw butter, salt and white pepper to taste.
Dilute with one-quarter portion of strong broth or bouillon, place on gentle heat and cook until the sauce is sufficiently thick.
Beat two egg yolks with {{source-8}} and season the sauce, which should previously be removed from heat so that the yolks do not curdle.

title: Sos Tatarski (Tartar Sauce)
description: A sauce made with egg yolk, mustard, and olive oil.
steps: Mix one egg yolk with one teaspoon of French mustard and salt in a bowl.
Remove yolks from ten hard-boiled eggs, strain through a sieve, add to the mixed yolk and blend.

Then squeeze juice from one lemon, or pour in about two tablespoons of strong vinegar.
Chop finely ten small pickles and ten marinated mushrooms, add to the sauce and mix.
Instead of mushrooms and pickles, capers and chives can be used; the sauce will be different but also good.

title: Zupa Rakowa (Crawfish Soup)
description: A soup made with crawfish, beef broth, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: meat from crawfish tails and shells
ingredients.sourceText: meat from crawfish tails and shells

steps: For four persons, cook thirty small crawfish with salt and dill, being careful not to overcook or they will be difficult to shell.
Remove the tails and extract the meat from the tails and soft mass under the shell on the body, using this for stuffing the shells.
Leave a dozen whole shells and place all the rest, as is, in a mortar and crush to a paste.
Take a spoon of good butter and crush again in the mortar together with the crawfish.

Place this mass in a pot and braise over low heat for at least an hour, pouring in previously cooked ordinary broth, and red crawfish butter will begin to appear on the surface, which should be collected with a spoon, strained through a sieve and poured into a pot in which a spoon of butter has been browned with a spoon of flour, mixing well together.
When the crawfish butter stops appearing, press the crawfish through fine cloth and allow the obtained liquid to settle; pour off the clear liquid from the top and discard the sediment at the bottom.

Pour the above liquid into the browned butter, mix well and dilute with sufficient broth, add some chopped dill and stuffed crawfish shells, bring to a boil, lighten with two spoons of sour cream, then put the removed tails into a bowl and pour the soup over them.

For the stuffing of the shells, proceed as follows: chop very finely the previously selected meat from the tails and shells, add grated bread crumbs, chopped dill, butter, nutmeg, salt and one egg yolk, mix everything well into a thick paste and fill the empty crawfish shells, well cleaned and washed.

As a side serve fried small bread cubes from white bread, or separately cooked small noodles rinsed with cold water.
Note: This soup can also be served hot.

steps: Chop finely 6 large tart apples, put in a pot, pour 3 cups of water and cook until the apples completely fall apart.
Strain through a loose sieve, add about 1/4 pound of sugar, 1 glass of white sour wine and zest from 1/2 lemon rubbed on sugar.
Whip 1 large cup of sour cream with 2 egg yolks, then slowly pour the hot soup onto this cream, stirring continuously.

As a side, serve small fried bread cubes dipped in cream and then fried in butter and sprinkled with sugar in the pan.
Note: Egg yolks can be omitted. This soup can also be made with pears in this way with the addition of a few sour apples, otherwise it will be bland.

Lightly brown one-quarter pound of sugar with two tablespoons of water over high heat.

title: A Nice Ice Cream
description: Prepared with cream, ice, and white sugar.

ingredients.name: a quart of nice fresh milk
ingredients.sourceText: a quart of nice fresh milk

ingredients.name: a pound of fine white sugar
ingredients.sourceText: a pound of fine white sugar

ingredients.name: extract, either of lemon, orange, peach or vanilla

steps: Put on the fire a stew-pan containing a quart of nice fresh milk.
While it is coming to the boil beat the yolks of eight eggs and a pound of fine white sugar.
When these are well beaten, take off the boiling milk, let it stand to cool five minutes, and pour it very hot over the eggs and sugar.
Strain this mixture, and add for flavoring any favorite extract, either of lemon, orange, peach or vanilla.
Let it stand to get cool, and pour it into the freezer and surround it with layers of ice, pounded fine, and coarse dairy salt, well beaten down.
Fill up till within a few inches of the top of the freezer.
Pour in one quart of pure cream, and beat it with a wooden spoon into the mixture in the freezer.
Turn the crank of your freezer briskly if you have a five minute freezer; if not, turn the can with your hand for fifteen minutes.
Pack round again with ice and salt.
Draw off the melted ice and salt water, and fill up again and set away to harden before serving.

title: A Spring Chicken
description: Prepared with chicken, melted butter, and salt.
steps: Select spring chickens for broiling. For a family of six several will be required.
Clean the chickens, nicely, singe, and then split down the middle of the back, laying the chicken open.
Break the breastbone with a mallet and flatten out the chicken.
Season well with salt and pepper, and brush with melted butter.

Have the broiler ready over a moderate fire, and place the chicken between the double broiler and let the fowl broil slowly for about a half hour, if the chicken is very tender, otherwise three-quarters of an hour.
Keep a plate over it all the time, as it will retain its flavor better.
Turn the chicken frequently, so that it may be broiled through and through.
It should be slightly browned on the skin side.
When done, place in a heated dish, pour over melted butter and garnish with chopped parsley and serve hot.
A garnish of cresses is very pretty. The dish is then called 'Poulet Grille aux Cressons.'

title: Almond Cake
description: A cake made with sweet almonds, citrons, and orange.
steps: Beat the yolks of the eggs and the whites separately, beating the latter to a stiff froth.
Blanch the almonds, and peel them and pound them to a fine flour in a mortar.
Grate the zest of the oranges and lemons or citrons, and mix well.
Beat the sugar and the yolks of the eggs to a cream, and gradually add one-half of the flour, beating well.
Then add the almonds, mixing thoroughly, and, after beating vigorously, add one-half of the whites of the eggs.
Beat well, add the remainder of the flour, and then add the remainder of the eggs.
